en: Mount Mayon in Albay is an active stratovolcano famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, primarily inhabits the dense tropical forests of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a unique freshwater lake located inside the caldera of Taal Volcano.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse coral ecosystems.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are ancient agricultural landscapes carved into the mountains over 2,000 years ago.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest nickel reserves, primarily mined in the Surigao region of Mindanao.
The Habagat, or southwest monsoon, brings heavy rainfall to the western parts of the Philippines between June and September.
Lake Mainit in Agusan del Norte is the deepest and second-largest lake in the Philippines, formed by tectonic activities.
